clue.text: Case of nun infiltrating peak event for ladies

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the nun's letters go into the word for peak

parts.note: a peak is a height, the highest point

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of nun are used

parts.note: the outside letters of nun, its first and last

explanation.surface: A nun turns up uninvited at a party high on a mountain held for women.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen night is a British term for a bride's party with her female friends before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a celebration attended only by women, typically a bride-to-be and her friends.

clue.text: Place no one wants to go? That guy will!

definitions.text: Place no one wants to go?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the underworld of punishment that nobody wishes to end up in
second meaning: the contraction of he will, written without its apostrophe

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as a reply to the first: someone is going there, and the answer is the contraction HE'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is the place of eternal damnation, and he'll is the shortened form of the pronoun plus will.

clue.text: Mexican snack from tin turned up at house

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A Mexican snack is found in a tin that has been delivered to someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually topped with cheese, eaten as a Mexican-style snack.

clue.text: Archaeologist in films upset ninja one said

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disarranged, so the letters of the three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A movie archaeologist is quoted as having distressed a ninja.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a link word introducing speech, but its letters are part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana Jones is the whip-wielding archaeologist hero played by Harrison Ford in the Raiders of the Lost Ark series.

clue.text: Loathing headgear friend regularly displayed

parts.note: a hat is a piece of headgear

indicators.note: only every other letter of friend is shown, starting from the second

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of friend

explanation.surface: Someone detests the hat a friend keeps wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing and hatred are synonyms, both meaning intense dislike.

clue.text: Circle area of water in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means read backwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a pool is a small area of water

explanation.surface: Someone draws a ring around a stretch of water, but backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed curve, so it can stand for a circle.

clue.text: Pope ran off, in theory

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Pope fled, at least theoretically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or theory but may not work in practice.

clue.text: Suffuse each chicken, say, with root of liquorice

parts.note: per means for each, as in ten pounds per head
chicken is an example of meat, as the 'say' signals

indicators.note: in a down clue the root is the bottom, so the last letter of liquorice is taken

parts.note: the last letter of liquorice

explanation.surface: A cook soaks every piece of chicken with liquorice root.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice root is a real ingredient, which tempts the solver to take its first letter; in a down entry the root lies at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through and fill something, which is what suffuse means.

clue.text: Road worker to laze around with one old man and boy (unknown)

parts.note: to loll is to laze or lounge around
I is the Roman numeral for one
pop is informal for father, one's old man
a lad is a boy
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A road worker slacks off with a father and a son, who remains anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: A lollipop lady is the British name for a school crossing patrol officer, who carries a round sign on a pole to stop traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: She works on the road, halting cars so children can cross safely near schools.

clue.text: Lout cried occasionally — that's clear

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only alternate letters are taken, starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of lout cried

explanation.surface: A yob shed a tear now and then, and that much is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid writing or thinking is clear and easy to understand.

clue.text: Account sent back about old soldier

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the letter for old
sent back means returned, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a report is an account of events

explanation.surface: A report has been returned concerning a veteran soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, especially in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Special roles arranged for astronomical event

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Special parts have been organised for a show about the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes between the sun and the earth and blocks the light, astronomers witness this rare sky event.

clue.text: One selling charm, ten bucks

indicators.note: bucks as a verb means kicks and jumps about like a horse, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A trader offers a lucky charm for ten dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' reads as slang for dollars, but it is a verb here signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant is a trader, someone who sells goods for a living.

clue.text: Catch parent dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone catches a mother or father in the act of dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to trap or catch someone, often by trickery.

clue.text: Insect — call entomologist initially to capture it

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the other letters surround the word it

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of entomologist is used

parts.note: the first letter of entomologist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks an insect expert to come and catch a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A termite is a wood-eating social insect that lives in large colonies.

clue.text: Whisky, say, I found during excursions to the west

indicators.note: the letter is found in the middle of the other word, placed inside it
in an across clue, going west means moving right to left, so the word is reversed

parts.note: trips are excursions

explanation.surface: On trips out west, someone discovered a fine whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is one example of a spirit, a strong distilled alcoholic drink, as the 'say' signals.

clue.text: Show anger with one getting married without license, at first

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the bride goes round the letter

parts.note: a bride is a woman getting married

indicators.note: at first means only the first letter of license is taken

parts.note: the first letter of license

explanation.surface: Someone is furious with a person marrying without the proper licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means lacking, but here it has its older sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to show resentment or anger, as a horse jerks its head back against the reins.

clue.text: Map-maker with vehicle got over rebuke by that lady

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word got is read backwards

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles
her refers to that lady

explanation.surface: A woman with a car was told off for driving over something.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartographer draws and compiles maps for a living.

clue.text: No difficulty over large picture holder

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed on top, so the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ease is the absence of difficulty

explanation.surface: A big painting is held up without any problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand on which an artist rests a canvas or picture.

clue.text: Group of animals caught, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: to have caught a remark is to have heard it

explanation.surface: A pack of creatures has been captured, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' tempts as trapped, matching the animals, but here it means heard, as in catching what someone said.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of animals such as cattle or deer that live together.

clue.text: Denies running after a strong scent

indicators.note: after means following, so the rearranged letters come after the a
running means moving about freely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denies chasing after a powerful smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Aniseed is used as a strong-smelling drag scent for hounds to follow, which makes 'running after' apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed has a powerful liquorice-like aroma, used in drag hunting as a trail for hounds.

clue.text: Part of church is surrounded by beer!

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside, so is goes into the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A section of the church is awash with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between the pews in a church, or a side section of the nave.

clue.text: Adolescent with some cigarette ends

indicators.note: some means only part of the words is used, so the answer lies within cigarette ends

parts.note: the answer runs across letters 8-11 of 'cigarette ends', spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A teenager is caught with a few cigarette butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is a teenager, a young person in their adolescent years.

clue.text: Embarrassed admitting bike is sent for scrap, perhaps

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
a cycle is a bike

explanation.surface: A shamefaced owner confesses the bike has gone to the scrapyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Recycled material is processed for reuse, and things sent for scrap are an example, as 'perhaps' signals.
